continuation_of: pure_engine_v2_steps.json (Steps 25-34 â€” engine hardening: data-driven config, second scene, frame-time visibility, automated tests)
status_note: This continuation tracker covers Steps 35 through 153 (Steps 25-34 remain in pure_engine_v2_steps.json). Steps 35 through 50 covered engine hardening continuation, data-driven hostile config, alternate scenes, depth sorting, entity roles, and stress-test validation; v1.0 froze at Step 100 and Steps 101+ are an additive Phase 2 continuation.

steps.name: Wire existing beep to new-high-score event
steps.definition_of_done: The existing single-beep round-robin fires when a run beats the stored high score, without adding sound assets or changing the audio API.
steps.notes: This is the smallest honest use of the current one-asset audio system. Collision-edge and GAME_OVER events already trigger the current beep through playNext(); the high-score branch now uses that same mechanism at the real record-break moment.
steps.implementation: In src/main.cpp, the high-score branch calls audio.playNext() before updating the in-memory score and saving it. No new asset, no new audio API, no sound-type abstraction was introduced.
steps.verification: Verified by Cyril: build succeeded, a full run reached 53.5884s and beat the prior high score of 47.7s; the console printed NEW HIGH SCORE and the beep was audible at that moment, alongside the existing catch/GAME_OVER triggers.

steps.name: Distinct event audio (game-over, high-score) + bug fixes
steps.definition_of_done: The project ships the runtime asset copy fix, the silent loaded-flag bug fix, and the one-sound-per-death UX rule: record death plays only win_sound.wav; normal death plays only GAMEOVER.wav. The tracker records the remaining known follow-up about the long GAMEOVER clip.
steps.notes: Packaging bug fixed: CMake now copies GAMEOVER.wav and win_sound.wav next to the executable, so the runtime path matches the game's 3-candidate asset probe. Silent-flag bug fixed: gameOverSoundLoaded and newHighScoreSoundLoaded were never set true after successful loadNamedSound() calls, so both sounds loaded but were immediately rejected by the playback guards. UX fix: in src/main.cpp, the caught-death branch chooses a single event sound per death, prioritizing the record-break cue over the normal death cue. Known follow-up, not blocking: GAMEOVER.wav is approximately 8.6 seconds long, longer than ideal for a game where deaths are sub-second; a shorter ~2-3s replacement clip is planned later but not yet implemented.
steps.implementation: In src/audio.h, set the event-loaded flags to true immediately after each successful loadNamedSound() call. In src/main.cpp, the caught-death block now only triggers win_sound.wav on a record-break and only triggers GAMEOVER.wav on a normal death. CMakeLists.txt copies both event asset files into the build output assets/ directory alongside the existing beep.wav and hostile_default.txt bundle.
steps.verification: Verified by build and runtime checks: PureEngine.exe rebuilt successfully, runtime logs showed GAME OVER and NEW HIGH SCORE events firing correctly, and the final run confirmed a record death played only win_sound.wav while a non-record death played only GAMEOVER.wav. The long clip length is noted as follow-up work rather than a blocker.

steps.name: Collision hit-flash feedback
steps.definition_of_done: A brief collision hit pulse is synchronized with the existing collision sound using the current render path, and the tracker records the investigated-but-deferred collision-perception quirk that the rotation-safe AABB is larger than the visible triangle sprite.
steps.notes: The flash uses the same edge event that already triggers the collision beep: when any new collision is detected, collisionFlashFrames = 6 and the render block overrides the active clear color for a few frames. Visual confirmation: the pulse reads as a quick hit-pulse, not a sustained tint. Investigated but deferred: the collision check itself is correct and loops player vs each hostile individually; the apparent bug is more likely a visual-perception mismatch because the rotation-safe hitbox is a 1.414x1.414 AABB while the visible triangle sprite is roughly 1.0x1.0. This remains a non-blocking known quirk for later debug-overlay work, not a gameplay bug to fix in this pass.
steps.implementation: In src/main.cpp, the anyNewCollision branch sets collisionFlashFrames = 6 and reuses the existing clear color override in the render block so the flash lands on the same frame as the collision audio cue. No new abstraction or subsystem was introduced.
steps.verification: Verified by runtime confirmation: the flash reads as a quick hit-pulse instead of a lingering tint. The collision investigation was reviewed from source: player-vs-hostile overlap checks are per-hostile loops, and the mismatch is a deferred visual quirk rather than a logic bug to fix now.

steps.name: Visually distinct hostile types via textureId
steps.definition_of_done: Hostile definitions can select a texture variant through an optional textureId, the value is threaded through Entity into the renderer, and the alternate scene visibly demonstrates textureId=1 while legacy/default data remains unchanged.
steps.notes: The first implementation pass exposed a missing data link: adding texture selection only to renderer.h was insufficient because Entity did not carry textureId. The completed chain is HostileDefinition -> lifecycle.h Entity construction -> Entity.textureId -> renderer.h per-hostile texture selection. The new assets/tex_hostile_alt.png is a 16x16 RGB texture matching tex_hostile.png's format, and assets/hostile_alt.txt uses textureId=1 for one hostile while retaining the optional 5th hostile value for backward compatibility.
steps.implementation: In src/hostile_data.h, HostileDefinition gained textureId defaulting to 0 and hostile= accepts either four legacy values or an optional fifth texture id. In src/entity.h, Entity gained textureId defaulting to 0; src/lifecycle.h threads each HostileDefinition.textureId into the hostile Entity. In src/renderer.h, tex_hostile_alt.png is loaded, managed, and selected for entities whose textureId is 1. assets/hostile_alt.txt demonstrates the new format.
steps.verification: Verified by Cyril with a real visual test: pressing 2 from the menu loaded hostile_alt.txt and displayed one orange hostile using tex_hostile_alt.png alongside two normal crimson hostiles. Pressing SPACE loaded the default scene, where all hostiles remained crimson with no regression.

steps.name: Win condition via configurable win_time
steps.definition_of_done: The game has an independent configured win_time target, enters a frozen distinct WIN state after the catch check, preserves endurance scores beyond the difficulty cap, and avoids conflating a normal win with a new-high-score audio event.
steps.notes: The win target is deliberately decoupled from maxDifficultyScale timing: both hostile scene files define win_time=120.0, so reaching the difficulty cap does not end the endurance run. GameState::WIN reuses GAME_OVER's frozen-world and SPACE-to-menu pattern with a distinct victory clear color. A UX bug was found and fixed: the high-score cue now plays in the WIN branch only when survivalTime > highScore as well; an ordinary win is silent because no dedicated win asset exists yet. A dedicated win sound remains future follow-up work, alongside the shorter GAMEOVER.wav replacement noted in Step 36.

steps.name: Consolidate texture-loading duplication in renderer.h
steps.definition_of_done: The four repeated entity texture candidate-array blocks are consolidated behind loadRgbAsset() without changing candidate order, loading behavior, or init failure handling.

All three retained unchanged because filename stayed 'GAMEOVER.wav'. Expected byte size for 2.5s float32 stereo 44.1kHz: ~882,044 bytes plus header/metadata; actual on-disk size after swap = 887,824 bytes (within ~5.8KB overhead of theoretical size â€” confirms ~2.5s at the claimed format). Build-time copy_if_different propagated the 887,824-byte blob into build/Release/assets/GAMEOVER.wav with a post-build timestamp, replacing the old 3,025,034-byte file â€” verified by dir listing before and after rebuild. Runtime sound quality (smooth fade vs abrupt cut) and perceived duration difference require actual speaker playback from a user session, which a headless build agent cannot verify.

(4) dir build/Release/assets/GAMEOVER.wav after rebuild = 887,824 bytes / 9/4 12:36 AM (freshly copied, mtime matches build run) â€” POST_BUILD copy rule worked. steps.name: Depth-based draw-order sorting in renderer.h
steps.definition_of_done: pe::Renderer::drawWorld sorts entities by Entity::depth before issuing draw calls (or applies an equivalent explicit ordering step), so draw order no longer relies implicitly on buildInitialEntities()'s construction order, while the current visual draw order (player, then scenery, then hostiles) remains unchanged for the existing entity set.
steps.notes: Source evidence only, no design pre-decided at drafting time: src/renderer.h:349-353 already named this exact gap in its own comment inside drawWorld: 'Step 45: draw order relies on the entity vector being in depth order... If a future step reorders the vector (dynamic spawn, removal), sort by entity.depth here before iterating.' Entity::depth already existed (Step 45, commit e1bee39) and was already assigned correctly by buildInitialEntities() (0=player, 1=scenery, 2=hostile), but no sort ever read it - draw order was purely accidental construction order. Broad-phase collision was explicitly excluded from this step: rendering order and collision performance are separate concerns per the project's no-premature-abstraction discipline, and bundling them was rejected during scoping. Design questions resolved during implementation (left open at drafting time): the sort runs every frame inside drawWorld (negligible cost at stress-tested entity counts, avoids cache-invalidation complexity); std::stable_sort is used so entities sharing a depth keep their existing relative order; the sort call lives in renderer.h, not simulation.h, per explicit instruction.
steps.implementation: src/renderer.h gained #include <algorithm> and drawWorld now builds a std::vector<size_t> permutation of entity indices, stable-sorted by entities[index].depth, computed fresh every frame before the draw loop. Neither entities nor colliding is reordered in place: the loop still looks up entities[i] and colliding[i] by the ORIGINAL index (the same i used by the still-index-based texture-select branches, i == 0 / i < 3), only visiting indices in depth-sorted order. On the current entity set this permutation is a no-op (construction order already matches depth order), so today's visual output is unchanged by construction, not by coincidence. No changes to entity.h, lifecycle.h, simulation.h, or main.cpp; drawAABBs (Step 42's debug overlay) was left untouched, out of this step's stated scope.
steps.verification: Release build succeeded (cmake --build build --config Release, zero errors, both PureEngine.exe and hostile_data_test.exe produced). hostile_data_test.exe: PASS. Visual/overlap draw-order check: manually performed by Cyril (the assistant cannot see the rendered window). The player was driven into a hostile and into scenery; correct draw order/layering held under actual overlap, not just at rest. This satisfies the definition_of_done's requirement that draw order/layering be confirmed unchanged.

steps.definition_of_done: Entity gains mass (default 1.0 - byte-identical when unset; mass <= 0 = infinite). resolveCollision dynamic-dynamic branch reworked to INVERSE-MASS WEIGHTING (the standard impulse resolution; FORMULA stated in the comment): invMass = static||kinematic||mass<=0 ? 0 : 1/mass; positional: pen * invMass/(invMassA+invMassB) along -n/+n; impulse j = -(1+e)*relVelAlongNormal/(invMassA+invMassB), applied as n*j*invMass each side. checkMassWeighting (REQUIRED headless, exact values): 1:1 = the original 0.75/0.75 equal split (byte-identical), 1:2 = 1.0/0.5 positional + impulse j=2.0 (a.vel 1->-1, b.vel -1->0), static-infinite = full 1.5 on the dynamic (unchanged P6), mass 0 = infinite.
steps.notes: The equal-mass assumption was ONLY in resolveCollision dynamic-dynamic branch (pen*0.5 split + impulse*0.5); the static branches already encoded infinite mass; the swept/fixed paths sweep statics only. No general rigidbody dynamics, rotational inertia, joints. Test fix owned: halfExtents default is (0.7071,0.7071,0) - the test now sets (1,1,1) explicitly (first ctest run failed on ALL FOUR asserts - a setup bug, not an engine bug). 2D non-regression: ctest 2/2, alive x3 True.

steps.notes: The parameter semantics were locked by existing tests (explicit -0.5/0/1/5 + no-arg defaults) - the override-when-explicit design keeps ALL existing tests unchanged (non-breaking). No rotational inertia, friction cone, joints, continuous contact solver, ECS. 2D non-regression: ctest 2/2, alive x3 True. First-try green.

steps.name: Physics: per-body friction (geometric mean + Coulomb tangent impulse)
steps.definition_of_done: Entity gains friction (default 0.0 - frictionless, byte-identical baseline). resolveCollision: COMBINED FRICTION = sqrt(fA * fB) (geometric mean, documented); the tangent = the PERPENDICULAR axis (normals are always axis-aligned AABB - no general 2D derivation); TANGENT IMPULSE: j_t = -relVelTangent / invSum clamped to +-friction * j_n (COULOMB CLAMP stated exactly), applied weighted by the SAME invMass values as the normal impulse (hoisted before the static branches - no second split); jn <= 0 = no friction (friction requires a normal force). applyFriction lambda called in BOTH the static branches AND the dynamic-dynamic branch (the missing dynamic-dynamic call was found by value diagnostics and fixed).
steps.notes: checkFriction (REQUIRED headless, exact): friction 0 = byte-identical to pre-207 (e=0.5 default baseline -0.5/0.5); friction>0 exact values (normal-on-Y setup: a.vel (1.625,0.25), b.vel (0.375,0.75) - tangential rel 2 -> 1.25, clamp 0.375); static vs dynamic (static unmoved, dyn.vel (1.5,1) per formula - test bug owned: dyn.friction defaulted to 0 and the geometric mean correctly killed the pair); MASS INTERACTION: 1:2 masses + shared friction -> the heavier body tangential dV 0.25 vs the lighter 0.5 (invMass weighting, same invMass values). No rotational inertia, joints, sequential manifold solver, ECS, 3D mesh binding. 2D non-regression: ctest 2/2, alive x3 True.
